BiblicalUsage: Madday means sufficiently, what is enough, and its one appearance is in 2 Chronicles 30:3, where the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently, so the passover could not be kept at that time. In the Hebrew text the word stands as two pieces, the question-word for what joined to the word for enough, which is why the indexes list it under its parts.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it as a sober warning: a passover delayed because the priests were not ready is a picture of worship put off for want of preparation.
